name: VIRELAI//ZERO
description:
VIRELAI//ZERO is an AI-composed neural music project launched in 2219 by Vantablack Media's experimental arm, Canticle Division, as a test of whether a fully synthetic artist could achieve authentic cultural traction without human creative input. The system was trained on 340 years of recorded music, with particular weight given to emotional-response data harvested from BCI listeners across all tiers — meaning it learned not just what music sounds like, but what music makes people feel and why. The result is something genuinely unsettling in its competence: VIRELAI//ZERO produces neural feeds of extraordinary emotional precision, melding quarter-tone melodic structures, layered polyrhythmic percussion, and long-form harmonic development in ways that feel simultaneously familiar and alien. Listeners frequently report crying without understanding why.

The controversy surrounding V//Z is substantial and ongoing. Human artists have accused Canticle Division of strip-mining the emotional labor of every musician whose work was used in training without consent or compensation. The system's defenders — many of them Vantablack Media shareholders — argue that the music's quality is its own justification. Canticle Division has carefully maintained ambiguity about which specific artists' emotional-response data was harvested, and several class-action suits have stalled in Meridian 88's corporate-adjacent judiciary. Despite the controversy, VIRELAI//ZERO's feeds are the most-streamed neural audio in Tier 3-5, and the project has generated an estimated Φ2.3 billion in licensing revenue since launch.
creator: Canticle Division (Vantablack Media subsidiary)
genre: synthetic neural ambient, AI-composed emotional architecture
audience: Tier 2-5 neural-feed subscribers; corporate wellness program participants; Tier 4-5 professionals who use it for productivity and sleep; people who are embarrassed they like it
cultural_impact: VIRELAI//ZERO has become the central flashpoint in Meridian 88's ongoing cultural argument about AI authorship, consent, and the commodification of human emotional experience. It is simultaneously the most commercially successful music project in the city's history and the most politically despised by working musicians. The phrase 'sounds like V//Z' has entered common usage as an insult meaning 'technically accomplished but spiritually hollow' — though this characterization is disputed by the project's substantial genuine fanbase. Several human artists have released work explicitly in response to or against it.
known_fans: people who distrust their own emotional responses to it
story_hooks: A musician recognizes something in a VIRELAI//ZERO feed — a specific emotional contour, a melodic gesture — that she believes came from a private recording session that was never released and should not have been accessible to any training dataset.

A corporate executive has been using V//Z feeds for sleep for six months and begins exhibiting behavioral changes that a doctor suspects may be neurological — raising the question of whether the emotional-precision engineering has crossed a line into manipulation.
Someone leaks the full list of artists whose emotional-response data was harvested for the V//Z training set, and a character has to decide what to do with it.
